<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

`/pij ready` is not stale — it runs `pij adopt` / `pij whoami` / `pij report`, and `pij` on PATH is the TypeScript CLI, so a seat reporting ready registers into the LEGACY store and is invisible to the rs daemon (observed live 2026-09-01: pij-fierce-xoxarle absent from `pij-rs list`). Two halves fix it. ROUTE (req-0011): one `pij` command that detects a live rs daemon and sends verbs there, falling back to legacy per-verb when rs lacks one — so nothing downstream learns a second binary name. PARITY (req-0010): implement the missing lifecycle verbs in rs, in the order real usage ranks them (PR #329's telemetry, not taste). Routing lands first so parity arrives invisibly, verb by verb.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Typing `/pij ready` in a fresh seat registers it into the RS store, with no skill edit and no human typing `pij-rs`.
- `pij whoami` names that seat from rs; `pij report now` writes its card to rs; `pij state <id>` reads it back.
- A verb rs does not implement falls back to LEGACY and still works — migration is invisible, never a cliff.
- The operator can always find out which generation served a verb, and can force either one.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No orchestration verbs (batons, projects, fences, streams) — telemetry shows they barely register; they wait.
- No consent-default change: crossSessionInbound stays opt-in (coupled to plan 110's held backoff).
- No data migration between the legacy store and the rs store — a seat lives in whichever registered it. If a seat must move, that is its own row.
- No rewrite of the /pij skill or any packet — if a doc must change for this to work, the routing design is wrong.

<a id="risks-assumptions"></a>

## Risks & Assumptions

RISK 1 — SPLIT-BRAIN IDENTITY is the headline risk: the same seat registered in both stores, or a seat that adopts into rs while its peers still resolve it in legacy, yields messages that vanish with every surface reporting success. Mitigation: routing is per-VERB but identity is per-SEAT — once a seat registers into a generation, every identity verb for that seat must resolve to the SAME generation, and the fallback must never silently re-home a seat. Name the rule explicitly and test it. RISK 2 — a fallback that hides a real rs failure: rs erroring must NOT fall back to legacy (that would mask defects and re-home seats); only rs NOT IMPLEMENTING a verb falls back. The two cases must be distinguishable at the call site — same lesson as F-1128 (a notice that cannot tell its cases apart carries no information). RISK 3 — the false friend (`tail`) silently serving the wrong object; retired by ac-1145. ASSUMPTION — the rs daemon's HTTP surface can carry the report/whoami/adopt semantics without schema migration; if a verb needs a store column, that is in fence and gets a migration test.
